h: Joseph Unites Torah and Covenantal Holiness

p: וַיִּישֶׂם בָּאָרוֹן בְּמִצְרָיִם.
— “He was placed in a coffin in Egypt.”
לִכְאוֹרָה תֵּיבַת בְּמִצְרַיִם מְיוּתָּר, שֶׁיָּדוּעַ שֶׁהָיָה בְּמִצְרַיִם.
— The word “in Egypt” appears superfluous, since it is known that he was in Egypt.
גַּם לְפִי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (סוֹטָה יג. וּמִדְרָשִׁים) שֶׁנְּתָנוּהוּ בַּנִּילוּס,
— Moreover, according to the teaching (Sotah 13a and the midrashim) that they placed him in the Nile,
וְהַנָּהָר מִתְפַּשֵּׁט אַף חוּץ לְמִצְרַיִם, לֹא יִתָּכֵן לְשׁוֹן בְּמִצְרַיִם.
— and since the river extends outside Egypt, the expression “in Egypt” seems inappropriate.

He said, “Joseph, Joseph! The time has arrived of which the Holy One, blessed be He, swore, ‘I will redeem you,’ and the time has arrived for the oath you imposed upon Israel. p: וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז בָּזֶה מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת בְּשַׁלַּח),
— It may allude to what is taught in Midrash Tanchuma, beginning of Beshalach:
שֶׁאֲרוֹנוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף מְהַלֵּךְ עִם אֲרוֹן הָעֵדוּת וְכוּלֵי,
— Joseph’s coffin traveled alongside the Ark of the Testimony, and so forth.
וְכִי דַּרְכּוֹ שֶׁל מֵת מְהַלֵּךְ עִם אֲרוֹן חֵי הָעוֹלָמִים וְכוּלֵי?
— Is it usual for a dead man to travel with the Ark of the Life of the worlds? And so forth.
הַמּוּנָּח בָּאָרוֹן זֶה קִיֵּים כָּל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בָּזֶה.
— The one lying in this coffin fulfilled all that is written in that Ark.
וְכֵן הוּא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ, דְּאִשְׁתַּוֵּי בִּתְרֵי אֲרוֹנֵי וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּן שָׁם.
— Likewise the holy Zohar teaches that he was equated through the two arks, and so forth; see there.
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהִנִּיחוּהוּ בָּאָרוֹן הָיָה מָלֵא דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה,
— Once he was placed in the coffin, it was filled with Torah teachings,
כְּמוֹ אֲרוֹן הָעֵדוּת שֶׁהָיוּ בוֹ הַלּוּחוֹת.
— like the Ark of the Testimony, which contained the tablets.
וְזֶה שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז בְּמִצְרַיִם עַל הַדִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה,
— “In Egypt” alludes to the Torah teachings,
דְּאָז הָיוּ כָּל הַדִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה עוֹד בְּמִצְרַיִם,
— for all Torah teachings were then still in Egypt,
כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהָיוּ שָׁם כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שׁוֹרֶשׁ שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא נְפָשׁוֹת, שֶׁהֵם שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הַדִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה.
— so long as all Israel were there, the root of the six hundred thousand souls, who are the root of all Torah teachings.

Shlomo HaKohen Rabinowicz of Radomsk, Tiferet Shlomo, On Festivals, Sukkot 60: “Therefore Yosef’s coffin went with the Ark of the Testimony as they journeyed in the wilderness, to say that this one fulfilled what is written in that one, as explained in the Gemara; the intent is that Yosef is the one who upholds the entire Torah, so that it endures within the children of Israel. This is why he did not command his sons to bury him in the Land of Israel at once, but ‘he was placed in a coffin in Egypt,’ and afterward ‘you shall bring up my bones from here with you.’ For he knew that he is the one who brings Israel out of Egypt and through whom they will merit to receive the Torah; therefore, when you bring up my bones from here with you, then ‘God will surely remember you’ with the commandments, for his bones are all holy like the Torah. This is ‘he was placed in a coffin in Egypt,’ just as there was an ark for the Torah. … For through the righteous one, foundation of the world, the whole Torah endures, and Israel with it, forever.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: The Tiferet Shlomo reads the same verse as Rav Tzadok: Yosef’s coffin in Egypt was an ark for the Torah, matching the Ark of the Testimony. He adds that Yosef’s bones are “holy like the Torah” and that his presence in Egypt is what prepared Israel to leave and receive the Torah.

h: The Holiness Hidden in the Bones

p: וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר שֶׁזֶּה מְרַמֵּז בְּמַה שֶּׁאָמַר וְהַעֲלִיתֶם אֶת עַצְמוֹתַי מִזֶּה.
— This may also be hinted at in his saying, “You shall bring my bones up from here.”
וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין לָמָּה לֹא אָמַר וְהַעֲלִיתֶם אוֹתִי.
— We must understand why he did not say, “You shall bring me up.”
וְאִם הָיָה דָן שֶׁבִּזְמַן רַב לֹא יוּשְׁאַר הַבָּשָׂר, מֵהֵיכָן יָדַע שֶׁלֹּא יֵרָקְבוּ הָעֲצָמוֹת?
— If he reasoned that after a long time the flesh would not remain, how did he know that the bones would not decay?
וְאִם עַל דֶּרֶךְ נֵס יוּכַל לְהִתְקַיֵּים אַף הַבָּשָׂר, וַהֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵימַר סְתָם אוֹתִי.
— If through a miracle, the flesh could also remain, and he should simply have said “me.”
אַךְ בָּא לְרַמֵּז קְדוּשָּׁתוֹ, דְּאִיתָא (נִדָּה לא.) שֶׁמִּצַּד הָאָב הָעֲצָמוֹת וְכוּלֵי וּמִצַּד הָאֵם הַבָּשָׂר.
— Rather, he came to hint at his holiness: it is taught (Niddah 31a) that the bones derive from the father, and so forth, and the flesh from the mother.
וְהִנֵּה כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהָעוּבָּר בִּמְעֵי אִמּוֹ אֵין בּוֹ יֵצֶר הָרָע,
— As long as the fetus is in its mother’s womb, it has no evil inclination,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין צא:) וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיִּשְׁלַח).
— as taught in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 91b) and the holy Zohar, beginning of Vayishlach.
וְהוּא בְּחִינַת בִּנְיָמִין, צַדִּיק תַּתָּאָה דְּלָא חָטָא כָּל יוֹמוֹי,
— This is Benjamin’s aspect, the lower righteous one who never sinned throughout his days,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק א׳ קנג ב).
— as taught in Zohar I, 153b.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִשֶּׁנּוֹלַד שֶׁשּׁוֹלֵט הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
— Once he is born, however, the evil inclination gains mastery.
אַךְ מִשֶּׁנִּימּוֹל, כֵּיוָן דְּאִתְגַּזַּר אִקְרֵי צַדִּיק,
— Yet after circumcision—once he is circumcised, he is called righteous—
זֶהוּ בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף וְהוּא בְּחִינַת צַדִּיק עִלָּאָה, וְהוּא מִצַּד קְדוּשַּׁת הָאָב.
— this is Joseph’s aspect, the higher righteous one, deriving from the father’s holiness.
וְיָדוּעַ דִּקְדוּשַּׁת יוֹסֵף הוּא הַיּ׳ שֶׁמַּשְׁפִּיעַ יַעֲקֹב בִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהִיא דָּלֶ״ת,
— It is known that Joseph’s holiness is the yod that Jacob imparts to the Congregation of Israel, which is dalet,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב ה׳ ד׳ הֲוַת וְנַעֲשֵׂית ה׳.
— as taught: the heh was a dalet and becomes a heh.
וְזֶה קְדוּשַּׁת יוֹסֵף לְתַקֵּן וּלְהִתְבָּרֵר בְּמִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם,
— This is Joseph’s holiness: to rectify and be refined in the attribute of the righteous one, foundation of the world,
אַף שֶׁכְּבָר שׁוֹלֵט הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מִשְּׁעַת יְצִיאָה.
— even though the evil inclination has already gained mastery from the moment of emerging into the world.
וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז עַצְמוֹתַי, עַצְמוּת י׳, שֶׁזֶּהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדוּשָּׁתוֹ.
— This is hinted at by atzmotai, “my bones”: the essence of yod, the root of his holiness.

h: Joseph Shares the Holiness of Jacob

p: וְאָמַר מִזֶּה לְרַמֵּז שֶׁכְּבָר זָכָה גַּם לִקְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
— He said “from this,” mizeh, hinting that he had also attained the holiness of Jacob our patriarch, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהוּא מֶרְכָּבָה לְשֵׁם הֲוָיָה, אַסְפַּקְלַרְיָא דְּנַהֲרָא.
— who is the vehicle for the Name Havayah, the luminous speculum.
שֶׁעַל זֶה מוֹרֶה בְּחִינַת זֶה, שֶׁמְּפוֹרָשׁ לְנֶגֶד עֵינָיו עַד שֶׁיּוּכַל לִהְיוֹת מַרְאֶה בְּאֶצְבַּע,
— This is indicated by the aspect of zeh, “this”: something explicit before one’s eyes, which one can point to with a finger,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב סוֹף תַּעֲנִית.
— as will occur in the future, as taught at the end of Taanit.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁזָּכוּ בִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף, דִּכְתִיב זֶה אֵלִי.
— Likewise they attained this at the splitting of the sea, saying, “This is my God.”
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר וַיִּישֶׂם בָּאָרוֹן בְּמִצְרָיִם, שֶׁהָיָה אֲרוֹנוֹ מָלֵא דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה,
— Of this it says, “He was placed in a coffin in Egypt”: his coffin was filled with Torah teachings,
שֶׁזָּכָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כָּלוּל בִּקְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה.
— for he merited to be included within Jacob our patriarch’s holiness, peace be upon him, which is Torah teachings.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א׳ קעו ב), וְיַעֲקֹב וְיוֹסֵף כַּחֲדָא אִינּוּן.
— As taught (Zohar I, 176b), Jacob and Joseph are as one.

paragraphs.text: Taanit 31a:9: “Ulla of Bira said in Rabbi Elazar’s name: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a circle for the righteous, and He will sit among them in the Garden of Eden. Each one will point with his finger, as it says, “On that day one shall say: Behold, this is our God, for whom we hoped, and He will save us; this is Hashem, for whom we hoped; let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation.””

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 176b; Zohar, Vayishlach 22:228: “Therefore the Shechinah is bound to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph. They are as one and have one form, as it is written, “These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph.” Therefore, “from all the merchant’s powders”: from the place of the river that flows forth, everything is watered and all faces are illuminated.”
